Impact: Entire threads feature (all 8 endpoints) unreachable in production; ThreadDrawer UI permanently broken; sweep endpoint cannot be called; docs describe a feature that does not exist at runtime.

Evidence: messages unique index messages_channel_sequence_idx is (channel_id, sequence_number) and is NOT thread-aware. Thread replies allocate a per-thread counter starting at 1 (thread-sequence.ts:21-25, message-local-store.ts:49-62) but insert into the same messages table with the channel id. Replica leg uses insert().onConflictDoNothing() (message-service.ts:497).
Reproduction: Insert 1 channel message (seq 1) in channel C, then 1 thread reply in a thread of channel C (thread seq 1). Replica INSERT conflicts on (C,1) -> onConflictDoNothing silently drops the thread reply from PG; no error, no outbox entry (failure path not triggered).
Root cause: Thread sequence space and channel sequence space both land in messages.sequence_number while the unique index is channel-scoped; onConflictDoNothing turns the collision into silent loss.
Impact: Thread replies are permanently missing from the PG replica (reports, RAG/context builders reading PG, multi-device sync); local tier still shows them, so drift is invisible.
Proposed fix: Make the unique index thread-aware, e.g. partial/expression index on (channel_id, coalesce(thread_id,''), sequence_number) via migration, and/or offset thread sequences per channel; keep onConflictDoNothing only after collision is impossible.
Required tests: Adapter test: append channel msg + thread reply with same logical seq, assert both rows exist in PG; migration test for new index; regression test for onConflict semantics.
Status: Fixed-verified 2026-10-07 (fix-threads): migration 0025 applied on scratch PG — messages_channel_thread_sequence_idx present + old channel-scoped index dropped + channel seq1 & thread seq1 coexist (thread-integrity.test.ts; THR_TEST_DATABASE_URL run exit 0); journal entry added so drizzle applies it; re-verified 2026-10-07 (fix-threads-flip-repair): vitest run src/threads exit 0; tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit exit 0

Root cause: TOCTOU window plus missing DB uniqueness constraint.
Impact: Duplicate threads per parent; ambiguous thread for a reply; client list shows two.
Proposed fix: Add partial unique index on threads(parent_message_id) WHERE parent_message_id IS NOT NULL (migration) and catch unique violation to return the existing thread; optionally do check inside the same transaction with a lock.
Required tests: Concurrency test with two parallel creates on one parent asserting exactly one thread row; migration test.

Evidence: messages.thread_id is a plain text column with no FK (schema.ts:297), so DELETE /api/threads/:id removes the thread but leaves replies with a dangling thread_id. Threads.md itself lists this as unverified.
Reproduction: Create thread + 2 replies, DELETE thread, then SELECT messages where thread_id = deleted id -> rows remain; GET thread messages -> 404 thread_not_found; replies unreachable via thread UI.
Root cause: No explicit delete rule was ever chosen for messages.thread_id.
Impact: Orphaned reply rows accumulate; thread UI reads break; channel timeline (which does not filter thread_id) may still show replies, confusing state.
Proposed fix: Decide one rule: ON DELETE CASCADE (delete replies with thread), SET NULL (promote to channel messages), or RESTRICT (block delete while replies exist). Implement via FK migration; align route semantics + docs.
Required tests: Integration test for chosen rule; regression: delete thread with replies asserts documented outcome.
Status: Fixed-verified 2026-10-07 (fix-threads): delete SET NULLs replies' thread_id then deletes the thread (thread-service.ts:232); scratch-PG test asserts the reply survives with thread_id null (thread-integrity.test.ts); re-verified 2026-10-07 (fix-threads-flip-repair): vitest run src/threads exit 0; tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit exit 0

Evidence: updateThread applies any status from UpdateThreadInput (type permits all three) with no transition guard: expired->active resurrection allowed; active->expired allowed with no expiresAt bookkeeping; archivedAt only set when status==='archived'.
Reproduction: PATCH /api/threads/:id {status:'expired'} on an active thread -> status expired, archivedAt null. PATCH {status:'active'} on an expired thread -> resurrected active with old expiresAt (sweep will re-expire next tick).
Root cause: Any-to-any transition accepted; no policy layer.
Impact: Inconsistent lifecycle state (expired without archivedAt, resurrected with stale expiresAt), sweep churn, audit ambiguity.
Proposed fix: Add a guarded transition map (active<->archived, active->expired; expired/archived->active only via explicit restore that clears/extends expiresAt and archivedAt) in the service; route surfaces 409 for illegal moves.
Required tests: Unit tests per transition incl. illegal ones; property test: after any transition, (status==expired/archived => archivedAt != null) invariant.
Status: Fixed-verified 2026-10-07 (fix-threads): guarded transition map — active→{active,archived,expired}, archived→{archived,active}, expired→{expired,archived}; illegal moves return illegal_transition → 409 (thread-service.ts:158; routes/threads.ts:73); archivedAt stamped once on every non-active move; scratch-PG + local tests (thread-integrity.test.ts; thread-local-mode.test.ts); re-verified 2026-10-07 (fix-threads-flip-repair): vitest run src/threads exit 0; tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit exit 0

Reproduction: Create an ephemeral thread with ttlHours=1, advance clock past expiry, wait: nothing flips it to expired because the endpoint is (a) unmounted (THR-001) and (b) never called.

Evidence: Sweep is a POST mutation with only global hooks: pinGate + authGate (loopback keyless trust). No route-level admin guard/secret. Once mounted (THR-001 fix) any loopback caller or any holder of a valid key can trigger mass expiry flips.
Reproduction: POST /api/threads/sweep from any allowed caller -> bulk UPDATE on all active expired threads.
Root cause: Endpoint treated as cron-only but carries no caller restriction.
Impact: Mass state mutation surface; a malicious/buggy local process can force expiry sweeps.
Proposed fix: Require an internal token/secret header for sweep (e.g. WORKSPACE_ADMIN_TOKEN pattern) or move sweeps entirely into the worker and drop the public endpoint.
Required tests: Route test: sweep without token -> 401/403; with token -> 200.
Status: Fixed-verified 2026-10-07 (fix-threads): WORKSPACE_ADMIN_TOKEN-gated admin preHandler on POST /api/threads/sweep (routes/threads.ts:41, :137); route test 401 no key / 401 wrong key / 403 viewer / 200 admin (threads-sweep-auth.test.ts exit 0)

Evidence: updateThread does getThread() existence check then UPDATE...RETURNING; destructured [updated] can be undefined if the row is deleted between the two statements; returns { thread: undefined } which the route serializes as an empty 200.
Reproduction: DELETE thread concurrently with PATCH: PATCH can answer 200 with empty body instead of 404.
Root cause: Non-atomic read-then-write; returning() result not checked.
Impact: Wrong success signal on a lost update; silent no-op.
Proposed fix: Make UPDATE conditional and check the returned row; return { notFound: true } when 0 rows updated (single statement).
Required tests: Race test (mock db) asserting 404 when row disappears between calls; unit test for update returning undefined.

Evidence: Message append commits (local or PG), then incrementCount runs as a separate statement with no retry/catch; a crash or transient DB error between the two leaves messageCount/lastActivityAt permanently one behind. Threads.md:106 documents the window.
Reproduction: Kill process (or force increment to throw) between append and increment; message exists, messageCount stale; no reconciliation job exists.
Root cause: Counter update is intentionally decoupled from the message write (no transaction available across local-first append).
Impact: messageCount/lastActivityAt drift; list ordering (lastActivityAt) degrades for threads whose last bump failed.
Proposed fix: Add a reconciliation path (recompute count on read or periodic job) and/or retry the bump via outbox; document counter as best-effort until then.
Required tests: Failure-injection test: increment throws -> counter mismatch detectable and repaired by reconciler.

Evidence: Malformed 'before' cursor (missing ';', bad date, NaN seq) silently degrades to an unfiltered head page instead of an error. Messages domain by contrast throws MalformedCursorError -> 400 (message-service.ts:149-158).
Reproduction: GET /api/threads/:id/messages?before=garbage -> returns the newest page (duplicate of page 1) instead of 400; a paginating client can loop forever.
Root cause: Lenient parsing chosen to be forgiving; no versioned cursor contract.
Impact: Infinite pagination loops / silently wrong pages; inconsistent with messages-domain contract.
Proposed fix: Return a 400 MalformedCursorError-equivalent (or reuse messages' parser) behind the gate; add contract docs + tests for malformed inputs.
Required tests: Unit tests: garbage/bad date/NaN seq/empty -> explicit error; valid cursor roundtrip.

Evidence: List cursor with ';' but invalid timestamp or empty id silently falls back to unfiltered head read (the if just doesn't apply the keyset clause). Numeric parse failure also ignored.
Reproduction: GET /api/channels/:id/threads?cursor=abc -> head page again (no error), duplicate rows to a paginating client.
Root cause: Same lenient-parse pattern as THR-011.
Impact: Silent duplicate pages; impossible to distinguish 'no cursor' from 'bad cursor'.
Proposed fix: Validate cursors explicitly and 400 on malformed; share one cursor codec between list and messages.
Required tests: Unit tests for malformed list cursors; contract test for roundtrip.

Evidence: listThreads returns only rows; no nextCursor/hasMore even though it clamps limit and supports cursors. The route returns { threads } only. Client (ThreadDrawer.tsx:116) never paginates.
Reproduction: GET list with limit=1 on a 2-thread channel -> 1 row, no cursor -> caller cannot fetch page 2.
Root cause: Half-implemented pagination: cursor input supported, output not emitted.
Impact: Clients cannot paginate large channels; hidden truncation at 200.
Proposed fix: Return { threads, nextCursor } (or header) built from the last row's (lastActivityAt,id); update route + docs + client.
Required tests: Pagination test: 3 pages roundtrip with exact page boundaries; stable order under ties.

Evidence: archivedAt is stamped only for status==='archived' (overwrites on re-archive) and never for manual 'expired' (the sweep path stamps it at line 118). Manual PATCH to expired leaves archivedAt null; archivedAt is overloaded for archive and expiry.
Reproduction: PATCH {status:'expired'} -> archivedAt null; PATCH {status:'archived'} twice -> archivedAt moves to the second time.
Root cause: Single timestamp column used for two semantics; no policy.
Impact: Audit ambiguity: when did a thread leave active? Inconsistent across paths.
Proposed fix: Either stamp a leave-active timestamp for every non-active transition (and never overwrite once set) or split archivedAt/expiredAt.
Required tests: Invariant test: any non-active status implies archivedAt != null; re-archive does not move the first timestamp.

Evidence: Threads service imports db/schema and reads channels and messages tables directly (validation + message pages) instead of going through Channels/Messages gates. AGENTS S2: Events/tables/queues have one owner domain; messages table is owned by Messages.
Reproduction: Code inspection; no lint failure because db/schema.ts is not a gated domain and the reads are via the shared schema module.
Root cause: Convenience access to shared schema; gates for channels/messages don't expose the needed reads.
Impact: Blast radius: schema/table changes in Messages/Channels silently break Threads; duplicated query logic (message keyset page duplicated from messages domain); domain isolation weakened.
Proposed fix: Move message-page reads behind messageGate (or a messages-owned port) and channel-existence checks behind channelGate; keep threads service free of foreign tables.
Required tests: Contract test: threads service works when messages/channels internals change (mock gates); gate lint rule extension for table symbols.
Status: Fixed-verified 2026-10-07 (fix-threads-015): messageGate.getThreadPage added in Messages (message-service.ts:556; raw rows keep threadId - the merged channel-page shape was not reused) and thread-service.getThreadMessages (local + PG tiers) now routes through it (thread-service.ts:252); direct message-local-store import removed. Evidence: node scripts/check-gates.mjs 0 violations; npx vitest run src/threads src/messages exit 0 (22 passed, regression thread-page-gate.test.ts); npx tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit exit 0.

Evidence: thread_sequences is bootstrapped by Threads but mutated by shared/core/thread-sequence.ts, which is called from the Messages domain append path. Two domains write one table; the allocator also self-heals missing rows, masking missing bootstrap.
Reproduction: Code inspection; table is written on message append by messages domain and on create by threads domain.
Root cause: Shared allocator helper predates the domain boundary; ownership never assigned.
Impact: Sequence drift risk if either side changes; hard to reason about invariants; violates one-owner rule.
Proposed fix: Give thread_sequences one owner (Threads): move the allocator behind threadGate (e.g. threadGate.allocateSequence(threadId, count, tx)) and have messages call the gate (gate-to-gate).
Required tests: Ownership test: only threads domain imports threadSequences; allocator contract tests via gate.
Status: Fixed-verified 2026-10-07 (fix-threads-micro-016-025): thread_sequences has ONE owner (Threads) - allocator moved to threads/thread-sequence-allocator.ts and exposed as threadGate.allocateSequence; Messages append calls the gate with its tx (message-service.ts:665, gate-to-gate); shared/core/thread-sequence.ts deleted; ownership test asserts only threads/thread-gate.ts imports the allocator and only db/schema + threads files name threadSequences (thread-fix-016-025.test.ts); gate contract test covers tx-bound reservation, self-heal from MAX(seq), batch start value; vitest run src/threads exit 0; tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit exit 0

Evidence: messageGate.append supports threadId directly and allocates thread sequences; any future caller that passes threadId without also calling threadGate.incrementCount silently under-counts. Today the only caller is the (unmounted) threads route, so the coupling is convention, not contract.
Reproduction: Grep: incrementCount callers = routes/threads.ts:108 only; append(threadId) callers = routes/threads.ts:100 only.
Root cause: Counter maintenance is caller responsibility, not encapsulated.
Impact: messageCount drifts as soon as a second append-with-thread caller appears.
Proposed fix: Move the counter bump into the same owned write path (messages domain notifies threads via gate, or a threads-owned use case wraps append+increment).
Required tests: Contract test: append with threadId always advances messageCount exactly once (incl. failure paths).

Location: packages/client/components/workspace/ThreadDrawer.tsx:161; packages/server/src/shared/sockets/register-socket-server.ts (no thread handlers; repo-wide grep for thread:join = client only)
Evidence: Client emits thread:join { threadId } on open; no server handler exists, no room join, no targeted delivery.
Reproduction: Open a thread in the UI: emit is silently ignored (server has no listener).

Evidence: No lifecycle events emitted for create/update/archive/expire; clients learn only via polling. Docs list this as a gap and the target standard forbids poll-only lifecycle.

Impact: UI staleness; no external automation hooks for thread lifecycle; audit trail absent.
Proposed fix: Emit thread:created/updated/archived/expired from an owned layer (route or, better, gate use cases) with the shared broker; register in event-types + check-events whitelist.
Required tests: Socket/event tests for each lifecycle event; check-events lint passes.

Evidence: List query orders by (last_activity_at DESC, id DESC) filtered by (channel_id, status); only single-column indexes exist (channel, status, expires).

Evidence: POST /api/threads/:threadId/messages has an untyped Body generic and no zod schema (unlike every other route in the file). Non-string content (e.g. {content: 123}) reaches content?.trim() -> TypeError -> 500; unknown fields pass through; authorId/authorName unvalidated.
Reproduction: POST {content: 123} -> 500 instead of 400; POST {content:'ok', authorId: ''} -> stored with empty author.
Root cause: Schema was skipped for this endpoint.
Impact: Raw 500s on bad input; inconsistent API error semantics.
Proposed fix: Add a zod body schema (content: string min 1, authorId/authorName optional with sane bounds).
Required tests: Route test: invalid body -> 400; valid -> 201.

Evidence: authorId/authorName are taken from the request body with defaults ('local-user'/'User'); any caller can post as any identity; authorLevel hardcoded 'stakeholder', authorType 'user'.
Reproduction: POST message with authorId:'agent-1' -> stored and broadcast as agent-1.
Root cause: Single-user trust model (loopback) extended to message authorship without checks.
Impact: Impersonation within the app; poisoned transcript/audit data; agents' messages can be forged.
Proposed fix: Derive author from the authenticated identity (when configured) or restrict authorId to a server-side allowlist; document single-user trust explicitly.
Required tests: Auth/isolation test: forged authorId rejected (when a key/PIN identity exists).

Evidence: Broker emit is wrapped in try/catch{} with a lazy dynamic import; any failure (including broker not registered) is swallowed with no log.
Reproduction: Disconnect broker; post a message -> 201 returned, no event, no warning.
Root cause: Defensive catch without telemetry.
Impact: Silent event loss; clients miss messages; no signal for ops.
Proposed fix: Log at warn on emit failure; keep delivery best-effort.
Required tests: Test: broker failure logs and does not fail the request.

Evidence: All thread functions resolve the DB from ambient AsyncLocalStorage (request-scoped x-workspace-id). No workspaceId parameter or SQL-level workspace predicate. Any non-HTTP caller (future worker/job/socket) that forgets runWithDb silently reads/writes the global/default DB.
Reproduction: Call threadGate.list('channel-x') from a worker/script without runWithDb: resolves global pool (default DB) instead of the channel's workspace DB.
Root cause: Tenant routing was implemented as an ALS side channel; domain APIs did not adopt explicit workspace context.
Impact: Cross-tenant read/write risk as soon as a non-HTTP caller is added; also affects the sweep job design (THR-007) - it would need per-workspace iteration.
Proposed fix: Thread workspaceId through gate inputs (or a context object) and/or enforce via dbForWorkspace; the sweep job must iterate workspace DBs like approval-sweeper does (forEachWorkspaceDb).
Required tests: Isolation test: two workspace DBs, same channel id shape -> no cross-read; worker-path test with explicit workspace.
Status: Fixed-verified 2026-10-07 (fix-threads-micro-016-025): every thread port takes explicit threadCallContext {workspaceId | db} - workspaceId resolves that workspace record DB via dbForWorkspace and fails closed (NO_DATABASE) instead of silently using the global/default pool (thread-service.ts resolveThreadDb); no-ctx path unchanged (ambient ALS bound by the x-workspace-id hook); worker-path test proves per-workspace handles (ws-a vs ws-b, same channel id shape) and fail-closed for a workspace without record DB (thread-fix-016-025.test.ts); sweep-side per-workspace iteration retained (maintenance-worker.ts:130); vitest run src/threads exit 0; tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit exit 0

Evidence: rootMessageId is always set to parentMessageId; the 'inherit root' behavior is not implemented (comment at 19-22 only covers dedupe). No nesting/root-resolution logic exists anywhere.
Reproduction: Create a thread whose parent is itself a reply (message with thread_id set): rootMessageId equals that parent, not the original root.
Root cause: Feature was never built; field kept for future nesting.
Impact: Misleading data model: rootMessageId promises nesting semantics it doesn't provide; consumers may trust it.
Proposed fix: Either implement root resolution (walk parent.threadId -> thread.rootMessageId) or drop the column from the contract/docs and mark it deprecated.
Required tests: Unit test for nesting (if implemented); schema/docs update otherwise.

Evidence: Gate-level create accepts any createdBy string (including ''), any title length, negative ttlHours (=> expiresAt in the past when ttlHours<0 and isEphemeral), and parentMessageId with whitespace; route validates but gate is the contract and other callers bypass route.
Reproduction: Call threadGate.create({channelId, createdBy:'', ttlHours:-5, isEphemeral:true}) directly -> thread with empty author and expiresAt in the past (immediately sweepable).
Root cause: Validation lives in route zod schemas only; service trusts input.
Impact: Domain contract weaker than transport; future callers create invalid rows.
Proposed fix: Move minimal validation into the service (createdBy non-empty, ttlHours >= 1 when provided, title bound) or export zod schemas through the gate.
Required tests: Service-level unit tests for each invalid input.

Evidence: Channel message reads filter by channel_id only - no thread_id IS NULL predicate - so thread replies also appear in the main channel timeline (both PG and local paths). ThreadDrawer separately shows them in the thread.
Reproduction: Post a thread reply, open the main channel: the reply is present in /api/channels/:id/messages output.
Root cause: messages table is shared; channel page never excluded thread rows.
Impact: Reply duplication in UI (channel + thread); may be intentional (Slack-style) but is undocumented and untested.
Proposed fix: Product decision: either filter thread replies out of the channel page (add thread_id IS NULL) or document the dual-visibility. Add tests either way.
Required tests: Pagination test asserting chosen visibility semantics.

Evidence: Two implicit cursor wire formats: list 'ISO;id' (lastIndexOf ';', keyset on lastActivityAt/id) and messages 'ISO;seq' (split ';', keyset on timestamp/sequenceNumber). Formats are stringly-typed, undocumented at the gate, and diverge from the messages domain's strict parser.
Reproduction: Code inspection; docs mention formats informally (Threads.md:101 lists them as a target, not a contract).
Root cause: No shared cursor codec/versioning.
Impact: Clients (present or future) cannot rely on a documented contract; format changes are breaking silently.
Proposed fix: Define and export cursor codecs (encode/decode + version marker) shared by route/gate; document in Ports.
Required tests: Codec unit tests incl. malformed inputs; cross-check with client pagination code.

Evidence: create returns the existing thread (created:false) even when that thread is archived/expired; route always answers 201 and drops the created flag, so a caller cannot tell a live thread from a dead one and may post into a 409.
Reproduction: Create thread on parent, archive it, POST create again with same parent -> 201 with an archived thread body.
Root cause: Dedupe branch ignores status and the response contract loses the created flag.
Impact: Confusing UX/API: caller thinks a new live thread exists; posting fails with 409.
Proposed fix: Return the created flag through the route (or 200 vs 201), and decide the policy for dead-thread parents (resurrect vs error).
Required tests: Contract tests for all create outcomes.
